latin: Si adulescentiam tuam in otio agis, senectutem tuam in labore ages.
english: If you spend your youth in leisure, you will spend your old age in labor.
The friend of fools is a fool.
The poet gives the rose to the girl.
The poet gives the roses to the girl.
I will give the books to the teacher.

latin: Propter hos avaros viros, civitate bellum gessit.
english: On account of these greedy men, the state carried on the war.

latin: Propter magnos animos paucorum virorum, hostes nostros vicimus.
english: On account of the great courage of a few men, we conquered our enemies.

latin: Is illos libros nimis laudavit, sed eosdem ipse scripserat.
english: He praised these books excessively, but he himself had written these same books.

latin: tu tecum istos stultos non debes iungere.
english: You should not join yourself with those fools.

latin: tu cum istis stultis te non debes iungere.
english: You should not join yourself with those fools.

latin: Is cum amicis saepe cenavit, et vitam adulescentiamque eius in otio egit.
english: He often dined with his friends, and spent his life and youth in leisure.

latin: Multas acerbas fortunas toleraverat; is autem vitam amavit.
english: He had endured many bitter fortunes; nevertheless, he loved life.
